ai.title: Fix backend Docker build and deploy config
ai.summary: Backend Docker build now uses `tsc-alias` to resolve path aliases into relative imports in `dist`, preventing "Cannot find module" errors at runtime. Entry point renamed from `src/server.ts` to `src/index.ts` across `package.json` scripts and Dockerfile. `deploy.sh` updated to force `linux/amd64` platform, switch VM machine type to `n2-standard-2`, and pin COS image family to `cos-109-lts`. `manicode/src/config.ts` adds `isProduction` flag to toggle WebSocket URL between localhost and wss://manicode.ai.

eli5.text: The backend server's startup code was renamed and its build process now converts shortcut file paths into real working paths, so the deployed server no longer crashes on launch with missing module errors. When the team deploys a new version, the server now runs on a more powerful machine type and builds specifically for the standard Linux environment, making the deployment more reliable. The config file also gained a switch that tells the server whether it is running in production, which changes the network address it accepts connections on. If you tested the server locally you might have seen it crash during startup because it couldn't find parts of itself; that crash is fixed. ai.title: Dockerfile sets NODEENV and copies .env
ai.summary: backend/Dockerfile sets NODE_ENV=production and copies .env alongside package.json. manicode/src/config.ts enables production check via process.env.NODE_ENV, switching websocketUrl to ws:// for production. Scope covers backend container config and manicode client settings. Note: insecure websockets (ws://) used temporarily in production.

eli5.text: When the backend service starts up in its production environment, it will now automatically load the application's secret settings file alongside its package configuration, and the client application will connect to the server using a less secure websocket protocol. You would notice this if you looked at the logs, which show whether the system is running in production mode, and if the client connects to the server at the production address using the insecure protocol instead of the secure one.

ai.title: Remove spurious common dependency from manicode
ai.summary: Removed invalid `common` dependency from `manicode/package.json`. Added `start-prod` script with `NODE_ENV=production`. Bumped package version to 1.0.2. Internal repo cleanup.

eli5.text: You can now start the manicode assistant in production mode using a new command, which sets the environment to production before running. The team removed an unnecessary package called 'common' that was listed by mistake and bumped the project version to 1.0.2. If you look at the project's package file, you'd see the version number is higher and the dependency list no longer includes 'common'. This is a behind-the-scenes maintenance change with no direct impact on how you use the assistant.

ai.title: manicode 1.0.7
ai.summary: manicode 1.0.7 fixes bin entry. dist/manicode.js removed. dist/index.js used. prebuild/postbuild scripts add tsc-alias. zod 3.21.4 added. Covers manicode/package.json. Build pipeline refactored for alias resolution.

eli5.text: The assistant's setup script was rewired to point at the main start file, so running the built command now finds the right place to begin. The packaging steps for shared code were reordered so alias shortcuts resolve correctly during build. If you ran the built command, it now actually starts the assistant instead of failing to locate the entry file. This is live today.
